meta.title: Move Safari Bookmarks to Chrome | Snug
meta.description: Export Safari bookmarks to an HTML file and import it into Chrome, with what happens to Favorites and Reading List. Menu paths verified {date}.

title: How do I move my bookmarks from Safari to Chrome?
directAnswer: Export your bookmarks from Safari to an HTML file with {fromExportPath}. Then import that file into Chrome with {toImportPath}. Chrome puts them in {toImportPlacement}. Menu paths checked {date}.

builtIn.title: The built-in method
builtIn.intro: Both browsers do this on their own. You need the HTML file and nothing else.
steps: Save the file. Safari names it {fromExportFile}.
If Chrome runs on another computer, copy the file there.
Choose the HTML file you saved and confirm.

carriesOver.title: What carries over and what is lost
carriesOver.intro: The HTML file is the only thing that moves. For Favorites and Reading List, see what Snug does with a Safari export below.
items: Left out of the file, per {fromName}: {fromHtmlDrops}.
Where a help page does not say, this page says Not listed instead of guessing.

withSnug.title: With Snug
withSnug.intro: Snug runs in Chrome and other Chromium browsers, not in Safari. Export the HTML file from Safari as above, then use Snug in Chrome for the import. Snug detects a Safari export on its own and keeps Favorites and Reading List apart.
steps: Install Snug from the Chrome Web Store.
Open Snug's Import page and choose the HTML file there, or drop it on the page. Do not use the popup for this: it imports at once, without a preview.
The Preview shows the detected format, the bookmark count and the folder tree before anything changes.
Use the checkboxes to pick single bookmarks or whole folders, such as Favorites or Reading List. Snug imports only what you select.

Choose an import mode. Create folder adds everything to a new Imported Bookmarks folder. Restore — merge puts Favorites on your Bookmarks Bar and Reading List in its own folder under Other Bookmarks, next to your existing bookmarks.
Leave Skip duplicates on. It leaves out any bookmark whose address is already in Chrome, and tells you how many it skipped.
withSnug.snapshot: Create folder and Restore — merge never clear your bookmarks. Before a Restore — replace, Snug saves a Safety snapshot to your Downloads and keeps a copy in Settings, so you can undo the import.

goesWrong.title: If something goes wrong
items: You cannot find the bookmarks after importing. Chrome places them in {toImportPlacement}.
Chrome does not accept the file. Check that you chose the HTML file Safari saved, named {fromExportFile} by default, and not another file type.
Reading List is not on your Bookmarks Bar. With Restore — merge, Snug keeps Reading List in its own folder under Other Bookmarks.
A bookmark appears twice. Open Duplicates in Snug: it groups copies by address and removes only the copies you mark Delete.

verified: Menu paths and file names were read from the official help pages of {fromName} and {toName} on {date}. Browser menus change between versions, so check the source if a path differs on your screen.
